## Definitions

- [statement] The documented connection choices are a connection string, an advanced-settings form that builds a connection string, and existing Atlas CLI configurations. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/connect.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration

## How it works

- [statement] Atlas connection troubleshooting distinguishes credential problems from DNS problems: check username, password, target cluster and authSource for authentication failures; an ISP DNS server that lacks SRV lookup support can cause DNSHostNotFound. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/troubleshoot-connection/ · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration
- [statement] The legacy `/query` workflow supplies the relevant collection schema to GitHub Copilot and asks the user to choose a collection when the prompt omits one. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/copilot-query.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code GitHub Copilot participant
- [statement] The historical /query workflow supplies relevant collection schema to Copilot, asks the user to select a collection when none is specified, and lets the user open generated queries in a playground or run them directly. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/copilot-query.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code GitHub Copilot participant
- [statement] Playground execution displays results in a Playground Results pane, or in a new tab if split view is disabled. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/run-agg-pipelines.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/require-playgrounds/require-local.md
- [statement] The historical investigation VSCODE-432 reports millions of Playground Loaded events per day and says the team temporarily disabled the Segment source and event tracking while seeking a cause; it does not establish a present-day event rate or root cause. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/VSCODE-432 · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code settings and telemetry
- [statement] The documented `mdb.defaultLimit` default is `10` documents when browsing a collection. ## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use `require()` to reuse local JavaScript code or load native and external Node modules in playgrounds. MongoDB documents a local validation helper exported with `module.exports` and imported by file path. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/require-playgrounds.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/require-playgrounds/require-local.md
- [statement] Use the Command Palette command MongoDB: Create MongoDB Playground to open a playground with sample commands. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/crud-ops.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/run-agg-pipelines.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For command-line script execution, mongosh documents `--file` or `-f` and recommends always using these flags when passing filenames because bare filenames can fail with other arguments. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongosh

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB for VS Code supports Atlas and self-managed deployments, including standalone, replica set, and sharded cluster hosts. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/connect.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration · also: https://github.com/mongodb-js/vscode, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/mongodb-for-vscode.md
- [statement] In Atlas, open the cluster Connect dialog and select MongoDB for VS Code to obtain the connection instructions; the Atlas documentation then directs users to connect with that connection string in the extension. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/mongodb-for-vscode.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration
- [statement] For replica sets, the extension recommends a replica set SRV record or Replica Set Name instead of a direct member connection: a member role change can close the connection or leave stale data. Direct connections to analytics nodes are unsupported. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/connect.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration
- [statement] In GitHub issue 1333, the reporter describes querySrv ECONNREFUSED with VS Code 1.132.0 and MongoDB Extension 1.16.1 on Windows while the same Atlas SRV string works in Compass. This is an attributed failure report, not a verified root cause or proof that all Atlas connections fail. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-07) — https://github.com/mongodb-js/vscode/issues/1333 · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration
- [statement] The extension documents encrypted storage of connection strings and credentials through the VS Code API. Microsoft describes its SecretStorage API as encrypted, platform-dependent storage whose secrets do not sync across machines. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/connect.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration · also: https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api
- [statement] Disconnecting closes the active connection and requires reconnection before further data interaction. Removing a saved connection removes it from both the current workspace and VS Code globally. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/connect.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration
- [statement] The legacy MongoDB Copilot participant generated MongoDB queries from natural language inside VS Code; Microsoft and a separate developer blog both described that integration. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/copilot.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code GitHub Copilot participant · also: https://code.visualstudio.com/blogs/2024/06/24/extensions-are-all-you-need, https://pascoal.net/2024/10/22/gh-copilot-extensions/

(low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/VSCODE-791 · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code GitHub Copilot participant
- [statement] MongoDB Playgrounds provide a JavaScript environment in VS Code for prototyping queries, aggregations, CRUD operations, and MongoDB commands. Saved playgrounds can document database interactions alongside application code. An output troubleshooting thread reports confusion between these destinations. - [statement] A November 2021 issue report says extension v0.6.10 returned `[COMMON-90002] load is not currently implemented for this platform` even though the reporter could use load in Mongosh 1.1.0; a maintainer replied that the implementation had not yet been exposed in VS Code playgrounds. This is historical evidence, not a current compatibility guarantee. ## Facts and statements

- [statement] The extension documents only one active deployment connection at a time; right-click a saved connection and choose Connect to activate it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/connect.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/commands.md
- [statement] If authentication is required, include database-user credentials in the connection string: the extension warns that an initial connection might succeed without them while data interaction remains unavailable. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/connect.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration
- [statement] For standard Atlas connections, allow the client’s address in the project IP access list and authenticate with a database user that has access to the desired databases. An Atlas application account is separate from a database user. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/connect-to-database-deployment.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/troubleshoot-connection/
- [statement] The extension includes an Atlas Terraform template; typing atlas in a Terraform file inserts a starting configuration. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/create-cluster-terraform.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration · also: https://github.com/mongodb-js/vscode
- [statement] The extension can connect to Atlas Stream Processing using a Stream Processing Workspace connection string. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/connect.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration · also: https://github.com/mongodb-js/vscode
- [statement] The documented advanced connection form does not support CSFLE In-Use Encryption or Kerberos Authentication. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/connect.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration
- [statement] The extension includes an Atlas Terraform template for creating a cluster; this is an extension feature, with provider configuration outside this concept’s scope. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/connect.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant, MongoDB for VS Code connections and Atlas integration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/create-cluster-terraform.md
